title: Hyperbolic Graph Topic Modeling Network with Continuously Updated Topic Tree

problem.claim: Linked documents exhibit hierarchical network structure, while document collections also contain hierarchical variation in topic specificity that requires semantically interpretable representations.

gap.claim: HGNNs preserve network hierarchy but do not model topics, whereas most topic models provide latent topics without representing semantic hierarchy.

contributions.claim: A Hyperbolic Graph Topic Modeling Network integrates network hierarchy across linked documents and semantic hierarchy within texts in a unified HGNN framework.
The model constructs a two-layer document graph whose intra- and cross-layer encoding captures network hierarchy.
For text decoding, the model employs a topic tree that retains semantic hierarchy and supports learning interpretable topics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Supervised and unsupervised experiments are reported to verify the effectiveness of the model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Document connectivity often forms a hierarchical network, and HGNNs are promising for preserving that hierarchy.
HGNN document representations lack semantic interpretability because they do not model topics.
Documents vary from general to highly specific topics, while most topic models assume flat topic structures.
The proposed framework combines network hierarchy across linked documents with semantic hierarchy within texts using a two-layer graph and topic-tree decoding.
The authors report effectiveness verification through supervised and unsupervised experiments.

source_observation.claim: Network hierarchy and semantic topic hierarchy are treated as distinct but complementary structures.

interpretation.claim: A representation-learning system may benefit from modeling relational structure and content structure jointly rather than forcing one hierarchy to stand in for the other.

application.claim: For linked-document tasks with interpretable themes, consider architectures that encode graph hierarchy alongside hierarchical topic representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this joint modeling is beneficial outside the reported supervised and unsupervised experimental settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe how the topic tree is continuously updated.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
